description: Math.hypot keeps the distance between two points in step with a move
code:
home = {x: 1, y: 1}
robot = {x: 4, y: 5}
distance = Math.hypot(robot.x - home.x, robot.y - home.y)
assert(distance, 5)
robot.x = 6
robot.y = 13
distance

description: Math.hypot measures the speed of a velocity from its three components
code:
velocity = {x: 2, y: 3, z: 6}
speed = Math.hypot(velocity.x, velocity.y, velocity.z)
assert(speed, 7)
velocity.z = 0
velocity.x = 4
speed

description: A class-level rule gives every point its distance from the origin
code:
class Point(x, y):
    this.x = x
    this.y = y
$Point.radius = Math.hypot($Point.x, $Point.y)
p = Point(3, 4)
q = Point(5, 12)
assert([p.radius, q.radius], [5, 13])
q.x = 9
q.y = 40
[p.radius, q.radius]

description: A mapping turns a list of moves into their lengths and follows a push
code:
moves = [{dx: 3, dy: 4}]
lengths = moves.map(move -> Math.hypot(move.dx, move.dy))
assert(lengths, [5])
moves.push({dx: 8, dy: 15})
lengths

description: Math.hypot stays finite where squaring large coordinates overflows
code:
big = 1e200
naive = (big ** 2 + big ** 2) ** 0.5
safe = Math.hypot(big, big)
[naive == Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY, safe > big, safe < 2 * big]

description: Math.hypot keeps tiny components that squaring would lose
An infinite component makes Math.hypot infinite even beside NaN
Math.hypot of nothing is zero and of one value is its magnitude
Math.hypot converts its arguments as Math.max does
An undefined argument makes Math.hypot undefined until it is defined
code:
target = {}
reach = Math.hypot(target.x, 4)
first = reach.value
target.x = 3
[first, reach]

description: A failed push rolls back a mapping that measures lengths with Math.hypot
code:
legs = []
lengths = legs.map(leg -> Math.hypot(leg.dx, leg.dy, rise))
failure = ""
try:
    legs.push({dx: 2, dy: 3})
catch error:
    failure = error
assert([failure, legs, lengths], [ReferenceError("rise is not defined"), [], []])
rise = 6
legs.push({dx: 2, dy: 3})
lengths

description: Drones within range of a moving base follow it through Math.hypot
code:
class Drone(name, x, y):
    this.name = name
    this.x = x
    this.y = y
base = {x: 0, y: 0}
$Drone.range = Math.hypot($Drone.x - base.x, $Drone.y - base.y)
Drone("near", 6, 8)
Drone("far", 15, 20)
inRange = Drone.filter(drone -> drone.range <= 10).map(drone -> drone.name)
assert(inRange, ["near"])
base.x = 12
base.y = 16
inRange
